title: Modi to India: Skip Gold, Work From Home, Save Forex
excerpt: PM calls for fuel restraint, a one-year pause on gold purchases, and a WFH revival as West Asia crisis rattles global oil markets.
body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi took the stage in Hyderabad on May 10 with an unusually personal ask for 1.4 billion Indians: change your daily habits, right now, to shield the country from a gathering economic storm. Tensions in West Asia have blocked around 20 per cent of global fuel supply through the Strait of Hormuz, and Modi made clear that India cannot afford to be a passive bystander.

**What Modi called for:**
His appeal spans reducing fuel use, delaying discretionary spending like gold purchases, limiting foreign travel, and reviving work-from-home habits that became widespread during COVID-19. He asked citizens to avoid gold purchases, especially for weddings, for at least one year — a striking request given that India imports nearly 700–800 tonnes of gold annually. On remote work, he argued that pandemic-era systems — online conferences, video meetings, WFH — had already proven effective and must be revived *'in the national interest.'*

**Why the stakes are high:**
India imports the majority of its crude oil requirements, meaning any prolonged disruption in the Middle East hits domestic fuel prices, transport costs, and inflation almost immediately. The country already spends an estimated ₹1,600–1,700 crore daily on fuel imports and stabilisation measures. State-run oil firms — Indian Oil, Bharat Petroleum, and Hindustan Petroleum — are collectively losing nearly ₹30,000 crore per month, and fuel prices are widely expected to rise by ₹4–5 per litre before May 15.

**What to watch:**
The government will monitor West Asia developments closely in the coming days, and a formal fuel price revision before mid-May could be the first concrete policy signal of how far New Delhi is willing to go.
